# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_016_page_001.jpg

---

1 For all these reasons, they were fittingly punished by similar creatures — tormented by swarms of vermin.

2 But for your people, you turned the tables entirely: instead of punishment you gave them a gift, satisfying their craving with something choice and delicious — you sent them quails.

3 The effect was this: the Egyptians, desperately hungry, were repelled from even necessary food by the disgusting creatures swarming around them — while the Israelites, after a brief period of hunger, feasted on extraordinary delicacies.

4 It was right that relentless deprivation should fall on those who were playing the tyrant; but for your people, the torment of the enemy was simply a lesson to observe from a distance.

5 For when the savage fury of wild creatures descended on the Israelites and they were being killed by the bites of writhing serpents, your anger did not burn all the way to the end.

6 It was a corrective shock, brief and purposeful — they were troubled for a short while, holding before them a sign of salvation, a reminder of your law's command.

7 The one who turned toward that sign was saved — not by what the eye could see, but by you, the Savior of all.

8 And by this very act you proved to our enemies that you are the one who delivers from every evil.

9 For the Egyptians were killed by the bites of locusts and flies — and no remedy existed, no cure could be found, because they had earned exactly that punishment.

10 But not even venomous serpents' fangs could bring down your sons — your mercy rushed to help them and healed them.

11 They were stung — but only to jog their memory of your promises. They were healed quickly, lest they sink into such deep forgetfulness that they could no longer make use of your goodness.

12 No herb healed them. No poultice. It was your word, Lord — the word that heals everything.

13 You hold power over life and death. You lead down to the gates of death and bring people back up again.

14 A man can kill through wickedness — but when the spirit flies out, it does not come back, and no one returns the soul that has been taken away.

15 But no one escapes your hand.

16 The ungodly who refused to know you were flogged by the force of your arm — chased down by freak downpours, by hail and unrelenting rain, and consumed entirely by fire.

17 The strangest thing of all: in water — the element that extinguishes everything — fire burned even more powerfully. The whole creation takes sides for the righteous.

18 Sometimes the flame was pulled back so as not to burn the creatures sent against the ungodly — so that seeing this miracle, the Egyptians would realize: this is God's judgment pursuing us.

19 Other times fire blazed right in the middle of water, exceeding the power of fire itself, destroying the harvest of a land gone crooked with sin.

20 In place of all that — you gave your people the food of angels. Without any labour on their part, you supplied from heaven bread already prepared, full of every pleasure, fitting every taste.

21 Your nourishment revealed your sweetness toward your children: adapting itself to whatever the recipient desired, it became whatever each person wished for.

22 Meanwhile snow and ice endured fire without melting — so that the Egyptians might know: the same fire that was sparing the Israelites' manna was destroying the Egyptian harvest, blazing inside the hailstones, flashing through the rainstorms.

23 And then fire forgot its own power again, so that the righteous might be fed.

24 Creation serves you, its Maker. It bears down for punishment against the unrighteous and eases off for blessing on those who trust in you.

25 So at that time too, it took on every form, obedient to your grace that nourishes all things — giving whatever each person in need desired.

26 This was the lesson for your beloved children, Lord: it is not the variety of the harvest that feeds human beings — it is your word that sustains those who trust in you.

27 Whatever fire had left unmelted, a passing ray of morning sun was enough to dissolve —

28 to teach that one must greet you before sunrise, approaching you at the first breaking of the day with thanksgiving.

29 For the hope of the ungrateful melts away like frost in winter and drains off like water that no one needs.
